title: Measure a foot form on a Brannock device: heel held in the cup, pointer to the ball joint, width bar to the foot
instruction: Measure the right foot form on the foot measuring device the way the device's maker instructs. Hold the form's ankle post so its heel sits against the back of the heel cup and stays there. With the other hand, slide the arch pointer along the inner guide until its curved nose rests on the ball joint, and slide the width bar in until it rests against the outer side of the foot. Then let go of everything and move both hands well away.
context: Shoe shops size feet on this device: it is still made and sold, and is described as still widely used in shoe stores (Retail Brew, 2024). The readings pick the shoe: the larger of the arch and heel-to-toe sizes, and the width at that size. The maker tells the fitter to steady the ankle and the device with one hand while the other works the sliders (brannock.com/pages/instructions-fitting-tips). A light printed form slides where a standing customer's weight would hold the foot, so the score latches to 0 if the heel is pushed out of the cup while the sliders are in use.
setup:
Station table with two arms. A Combination Brannock Device lies across the table, heel cup toward the left arm, toe end toward the right arm, inner (medial) guide on the far side; its base is taped to the table. Its heel cup's back wall, on the centre line, is at x 0.29 m, y 0.13 m. Device outline, heel cup and slider shapes are modelled from the maker's photos and patents (dimensions in the README). Scales follow the published sizing rule: arch scale on the guide top, length scale under the toes, width chart beyond the toes read at the width bar's red index line. The arch pointer starts slid back (index at 146 mm from the cup's back wall) and the width bar at its widest (128 mm from the guide face), as the maker says to prepare it. Each slider carries a printed PLA grasp tab (a 24 x 5 x 24 mm fin on a 30 x 12 x 2 mm flange, STL in the task folder) stuck to its top with the mounting tape.

Foot form (rigid PLA right foot, printed from the STL in the task folder; own design with a rounded heel, arch, ball bulges, five toes and a 60 mm round ankle post whose top is 130 mm above the sole). Trial k uses layout k mod 3:
- 0: men's 8 C: 254.0 mm long, heel-to-ball 180.8 mm, ball width 90.5 mm, 229 g; heel 22 mm forward of the cup's back wall, 3 mm toward the outer side, toes out 1.5 deg.
- 1: men's 9 D: 262.5 mm, 186.4 mm, 98.4 mm, 251 g; heel 28 mm forward, 4 mm outward, toes out 2 deg.
- 2: men's 10 1/2 E: 275.2 mm, 194.8 mm, 108.0 mm, 284 g; heel 25 mm forward, 2 mm outward, toes out 1 deg.
On every form the inner ball bulge is 52 mm from the heel's centre line. Reference readings: the published table's arch size and width letter for the form. Real trials set each start pose with the printed placement card for the layout (task folder).
scoring:
Scored at the end. Thresholds: heel seated = a 3 mm feeler does not fit behind the heel at the cup's centre; a slider on the foot = the 3 mm feeler does not fit between the pointer's curve (or the bar's face) and the foot; width reading within one width letter of the reference; arch reading within half a size; references are the published Brannock table values for the form's size and width. Not held = no gripper within 20 mm.
- 0.25: heel seated with the form not held, and at least one slider on the foot and not held.
- 0.5: as 0.25, with that slider's reading within tolerance.
- 0.75: heel seated with the form not held; both sliders on the foot, not held, both readings within tolerance.
- 1.0: all of 0.75, every gripper 50 mm or more from the form, pointer and bar, and still for 1 s: form below 5 mm/s and 3 deg/s, each slider below 2 mm/s (in 20 fps video: the form moves under 5 mm and each slider under 2 mm over the last 20 frames).
Seating the heel alone scores 0.
Latched 0 at any moment: the form falls onto the table; its ankle post tips more than 20 deg from vertical; or, once the heel has been seated and a slider has since moved 2 mm from its start, the heel comes 10 mm or more off the cup's back wall.
Checks: 3 mm feeler gauge, the device's scales, photo, trial video.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted demo takes 669 to 699 steps
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the next trial's form on its start marks (heel position and offset per layout, a pencil line on the plate), slide the pointer back to 146 mm and the width bar out to its widest.
fidelity: Rigid PLA forms stand in for a foot; length, heel-to-ball and ball width follow the published Brannock table. Device body, heel cup and slider shapes are modelled, not published by the maker (the pointer's curve is modelled flush with the guide face). Sliders are free prismatic joints with Coulomb friction, moved only by contact. The base is fixed (taped in real trials). A light form slides where a standing customer's foot would not; the heel-out latch scores that.
scores: Dream-1 run (trial 0): 0.0, both grippers reached over the form and withdrew without seating the heel with a slider on the foot. Scripted closed-loop demo: 1.0 on every layout, three runs each (669, 699 and 678 steps).
